acceptance: Stub-CLI tests: after a wrapped run the machine is stopped whether it was running, stopped or unknown before; BENCHBOX_KEEP_LINUX_MACHINE=1 leaves its prior state; a live foreign `container machine run -n m` (and a nameless one when m is default) prevents the stop and is logged; the run's exit code is preserved. The tests that pinned the old rule (test_a_machine_that_was_already_running_is_left_running, test_an_unknown_prior_state_is_never_stopped) are rewritten.
Matcher test with real argv shapes (`-n m`, `--name m`, nameless with default true and false, `create`, `-d`, another machine name) through the function the production reader uses.

Sentinel tests with injected readings: an idle machine past the window with no matching process and no holder tree containing the wrapper is stopped once; a live holder running an unrelated command does not protect it; a holder tree containing the wrapper, a live matching process, or being inside the window does; warn mode stops nothing; another machine is never touched; a stop failure or timeout is logged and retried only after the next window; with `container` absent the check is a no-op.
heavy-status tests: the idle-VM flag appears only when the machine is running with no protecting holder; an unguarded run is reported.

Smoke (owner present): `BENCHBOX_HEAVY_WATCHDOG=warn BENCHBOX_HEAVY_VM_IDLE_MINUTES=0 make heavy-sentinel SENTINEL_ARGS='--duration 30 --log /tmp/s.log'` logs the idle-VM line and does not stop the machine; `make heavy-status` shows the flag.
make comment-policy-check, lint, typecheck, makefile-inventory-check, test-fast pass.

description:
Problem: the Linux VM can stay resident (8 GiB reserved) with nothing holding the host lock. scripts/linux_machine_run.sh restores the machine's prior state, so a machine already running stays up; hand-started `container machine run`/`create` bypasses the guard; the documented setup (`container machine create`) leaves the VM running; the sentinel ignores VMs.

Change:
1. scripts/linux_machine_run.sh stops the machine after every run, whatever its prior state (including unknown), unless BENCHBOX_KEEP_LINUX_MACHINE=1, or unless another same-user host process (not its own child) is running `container machine run`/`create` against this machine (`-n <m>`/`--name <m>`, or no name when the machine is `default: true`). In that case log 'left running: in use by pid N' and leave reclaiming to the sentinel. If the process check cannot run, stop.
2. A dedicated psutil reader and argv matcher find same-user `container machine run`/`create` processes for the machine and bash processes running scripts/linux_machine_run.sh with the machine as argument (heavy_sentinel.read_processes' prefilter drops `container` and `bash`, so it cannot be reused).
3. The sentinel stops the machine when it is running, no live lock holder's tree (heavy_sentinel.held_tree_pids) contains scripts/linux_machine_run.sh or a `container machine run` for it, and no matching process has been seen for BENCHBOX_HEAVY_VM_IDLE_MINUTES (default 10). Re-check processes and holders immediately before stopping. `container machine stop` gets a 60 s timeout and runs without blocking memory checks for more than one interval; a failure or timeout is logged and retried no sooner than the next idle window. Warn mode reports only.
4. Settings use the BENCHBOX_HEAVY_ prefix (BENCHBOX_HEAVY_LINUX_MACHINE, BENCHBOX_HEAVY_VM_IDLE_MINUTES) so sentinel_launchd forwards them to the LaunchAgent.
5. make heavy-status flags 'VM running with no lock holder' (machine name, state, configured memory) and prints the remedy `container machine stop <machine>`; heavy-status and the sentinel report 'UNGUARDED VM RUN pid N' for a live `container machine run`/`create` against the machine outside every holder's tree (report only, never signal).
6. The setup text (Makefile ci-linux setup message, scripts/linux_preflight_pytest.sh setup message) appends `container machine stop <machine>` after `create`.
7. Amend [HEAVY-LOCK-001] in docs/agent/heavy-work.md ('Never stop, resize, or signal a process or VM you did not start') with an exception: scripts/linux_machine_run.sh and the sentinel stop the machine named by BENCHBOX_HEAVY_LINUX_MACHINE under the conditions above. Add the rule that interactive VM use goes through `make heavy-run CMD='bash scripts/linux_machine_run.sh benchbox-agent -- <cmd>'`. Update Known limits (a SIGKILLed wrapper skips the EXIT trap; `run -d` guest processes are invisible to the host; BENCHBOX_KEEP_LINUX_MACHINE=1 leaves the machine to the idle reclaim), tests/README.md heavy-work sections, and the ci-linux stderr note. Changelog fragment.

Decision gates:
- G1: `container machine --help` (CLI 1.1.0) shows run boots on demand. Record the observed stop duration and next-boot success during the owner smoke; stop and record if either fails.
- G2 (owner gate): the sentinel acts only once installed; this Mac had no LaunchAgent on 2026-11-01. The PR asks the owner to run `make heavy-sentinel-install`; closeout records `make heavy-status` showing 'sentinel: running' or notes it as pending. Until then the next guarded run stops an idle machine on exit.
- G3 (owner approval): the [HEAVY-LOCK-001] exception is a policy change; record the owner's approval in the PR.

Guardrails: linked worktree via make worktree-create; stage paths explicitly. [COMMENT-POLICY-001]: no comments or docstrings. Tests use stub `container` executables, tmp BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_DIR, injected process tables and readings; never touch the real lock, never start, stop or resize a real VM from tests. Act only on the machine named by BENCHBOX_HEAVY_LINUX_MACHINE (default benchbox-agent, matching the Makefile CI_LINUX_MACHINE default); never touch other machines (e.g. ss-dev) or containers. `container` CLI 1.1.0 machine subcommands: create (creates and boots), delete, inspect, list, logs, run (boots on demand; no -n targets the default machine), set, set-default, stop. There is no start or exec. When `container` is not on PATH (Linux CI, Windows) every VM check is a silent no-op.
